1.overview: Zechariah recounts the LORD’s call for Judah to return, contrasting the people’s disobedient ancestors with the fulfillment of the LORD’s words. In visions, horsemen report that the earth is at rest as the LORD promises mercy and restoration for Jerusalem, then four horns that scattered Judah are opposed by four craftsmen.

sections.heading: Call to Return to the LORD

2.overview: Zechariah sees a man measuring Jerusalem, and an angel announces that the city will grow beyond its walls, with the LORD as its protection and glory. The LORD calls the exiles to flee Babylon, promises judgment on those who plundered them, and declares that he will dwell among Zion, gather many nations, and again choose Jerusalem and Judah.

3.overview: Zechariah sees Joshua the high priest accused by Satan before the angel of the LORD, who rebukes Satan and replaces Joshua’s filthy garments with clean robes and a turban. The angel charges Joshua to keep the LORD’s instructions and announces the Branch, a stone, the removal of the land’s iniquity in one day, and peace under vine and fig tree.

sections.heading: Joshua’s Charge and the Coming Branch

4.overview: An angel awakens Zechariah and shows him a gold lampstand supplied by two olive trees, then explains that Zerubbabel will complete the temple not by human might but by the LORD’s Spirit. The angel says obstacles will give way, the LORD will rejoice over Zerubbabel’s work, and the two olive trees represent two anointed ones standing beside the Lord of all the earth.

5.overview: Zechariah sees a flying scroll that carries a curse against thieves and those who swear falsely, entering their houses and destroying them. He then sees a woman called Wickedness confined in a measuring basket and carried by two women to Shinar, where a house is to be built for it.

sections.heading: The flying scroll and its curse

6.overview: Zechariah sees four chariots emerge from between bronze mountains and learns that they are the four spirits of heaven sent to patrol the earth; those going north give rest to the LORD’s Spirit there. The LORD directs Zechariah to crown Joshua the high priest and proclaim the Branch, who will build the temple and rule as both king and priest, while people from far away will help build it if the people obey the LORD.

sections.heading: The Four Chariots and Their Mission
Joshua Crowned and the Branch Announced

7.overview: In the fourth year of Darius, messengers from Bethel ask whether they should continue the fifth-month fast, and the LORD questions whether the people’s past fasting and feasting were done for him. The LORD recalls the earlier call to justice and compassion, then describes how the people refuse to listen and are scattered, leaving the land desolate.

sections.heading: The Call to Justice and Compassion

8.overview: The LORD of Hosts promises to return to Zion, restore Jerusalem, gather the people, and replace hardship with safety and abundance. He calls for truth and justice, declares that Judah’s fasts will become feasts, and describes nations coming to seek the LORD in Jerusalem.

sections.heading: Zion Restored and the People Gathered
Fasts Become Feasts and Nations Come

9.overview: The LORD announces judgment against Hadrach, Damascus, Hamath, Tyre, Sidon, and the Philistine cities, while making a remnant of the Philistines and guarding Jerusalem. Zion’s humble king brings peace to the nations, and the LORD releases prisoners, empowers Judah and Ephraim against Greece, and saves and restores his people.

10.overview: The LORD calls the people to seek rain from Him rather than trust idols and false diviners, then promises to punish failed shepherds and strengthen Judah and Joseph for battle. He promises to gather and restore the scattered people from distant lands, bring down Assyria and Egypt, and strengthen them in His name.

sections.heading: Rain and False Sources of Help
The Scattered People Gathered and Restored

11.overview: The chapter depicts Lebanon’s forests and the shepherds’ glory in ruin, then announces that the flock marked for slaughter will be abandoned to hostile rulers. The prophet pastures the flock with staffs named Favor and Union, breaks them to signify the revocation of a covenant and the division of Judah and Israel, receives thirty pieces of silver, and pronounces judgment on a worthless shepherd.

12.overview: The LORD declares that the nations gathering against Jerusalem will be injured and defeated, while he protects Jerusalem and strengthens Judah. He pours out a spirit of grace and prayer on the house of David and Jerusalem, and the people mourn the pierced one with grief compared to the mourning at Hadad-rimmon and Megiddo.

sections.heading: Jerusalem and Judah against the nations

13.overview: The LORD promises a fountain for cleansing the house of David and Jerusalem, the removal of idols and false prophets, and the exposure of those who falsely prophesy. The LORD calls the sword against His Shepherd, says the sheep will scatter and most of the land will perish, and promises to refine the surviving third and renew their covenant relationship.

sections.heading: Cleansing and the Removal of False Prophets
The Shepherd, Judgment, and the Refined Remnant

14.overview: The LORD gathers the nations against Jerusalem, then fights them and brings deliverance as the Mount of Olives splits, living water flows from the city, and the LORD reigns over the earth. The nations face judgment and survivors worship the LORD in Jerusalem, while the city and its vessels become holy to Him.

sections.heading: Jerusalem Renewed Under the LORD’s Rule
Judgment on the Nations and Their Worship
